new_task_1.title: Allow HTTP/2 responses to be closed
new_task_1.description: The 2.2.1 update adds a close method to urllib3's experimental HTTP2Response class. This makes HTTP/2 response objects compatible with response cleanup paths that call close, instead of falling back to an unimplemented base response close behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure urllib3 HTTP/2 response objects can be closed through the normal response interface without raising an unimplemented-method error.

expectation.grounded: HTTP2Response should define a close() method that can be called and returns normally. The method does not need to perform additional cleanup work in this implementation.
expectation.conceptual: Callers and internal cleanup code should be able to treat HTTP/2 responses like other response objects for close operations, even when there is no extra HTTP/2-specific resource cleanup to perform.

constraints.grounded: Do not change HTTP/2 response reading, status/header parsing, redirect handling, or body data behavior. The close implementation should be a no-op that preserves the existing response state.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only fill the missing close interface for HTTP/2 responses and should not introduce new lifecycle semantics beyond allowing close calls to succeed.

behavior: HTTP2Response exposes a callable close() method.
Calling HTTP2Response.close() returns normally without raising NotImplementedError or another missing-method failure.
Calling close() does not alter HTTP/2 response status, headers, body data, or redirect behavior.
Internal or external response cleanup paths that invoke close() on an HTTP/2 response can complete successfully.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HTTP2Response instance, when close() is called, then the call should complete without raising an unimplemented-method error.

Given cleanup code that calls close() on a response object returned by urllib3's HTTP/2 support, when the response is an HTTP2Response, then cleanup should not fail solely because the response lacks a close implementation.
Given an HTTP2Response instance, when close() is called, then existing status, headers, response data, and redirect-location behavior should remain unchanged.
